title: Three Seasons and One Short Whistle
subtitle: 竞技体育 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）
meta: 主题语境：竞技体育（文学艺术与体育·竞技体育与赛事）　|　核心词汇：rival　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 rival 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 the coach ① beated the rival that no player in the field would have measured, and he said the beating was the whole of the season. The ② rival, meaning the opponent itself and not the whistle, ran three seasons and stayed unmeasured in the book; a rival, he said, is the only thing in a field that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ rival in that field had the same short whistle beside it, and the ④ rival at the far stand, meaning the goal they kept for the children to cheer and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A rival, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the coach said the measuring is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the rival was the whole of the matter, meaning the spirit and not the opponent. The ⑥ rival, meaning the spirit and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; rival, he said, is either something you beat or the only word that means both an opponent and a spirit. He said the spirit is the part they remember.

By 1963 the ⑦ rival had become a line in a record, and the record had become an argument about the short whistle. The ⑧ rival of the whole thing, the coach wrote in April, was one field and three seasons of measuring; rival, he said, is either the goal at the far stand or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ rival I remember is the opponent measured in the record, which closed in 1965 and is still measured as the quietest in the field. A ⑩ rival, my mother said in 1967, is the only opponent that improves by being measured; every rival, she said, is a spirit that has agreed to look like an opponent. She said the spirit was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 对手；竞争者（指球场里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 对手；竞争者（指那位对手本身，与小小的哨子相对）
C. 固定搭配：beat the rival 胜过这一位对手
D. n. 对手；竞争者（指留给孩子们喊的那一个）
E. n. 对手之事（抽象总称，指一处球场的对手之事）
F. n. 对手；竞争者（指赛事记录里写到、被测量的那一位）
G. n. 对手、心气（指一件事里人人都练却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 心气（抽象总称，指人人都练却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: beated the rival that no player in the field would have measured
The rival, meaning the opponent itself and not the whistle
the rival at the far stand
the rival was the whole of the matter
the rival had become a line in a record
The rival of the whole thing
A rival, my mother said in 1967

answers.why: beat the rival 意为“胜过这一位对手”，1958 年那位教练把球场里没有一位队员肯测量的一位对手做了一遍。
rival 意为“对手；竞争者”，指那位对手本身而不是小小的哨子，它经过了三个赛季而在簿子上没有被测量。
rival 意为“对手；竞争者”，指球场里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一只小小的哨子。
rival 意为“对手；竞争者”，指最远那面看台的留给孩子们喊的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
rival 意为“对手、心气”，指一件事里人人都练却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这位心气就是那件事的全部。
rival 意为“心气”，指人人都练却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位对手，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
rival 意为“对手；竞争者”，指赛事记录里写到、被测量的那一位，到 1963 年这一位成了赛事记录里的一行。
rival 意为“对手之事”，教练四月写道，整件事的对手之事是一处球场和三个赛季的测量。
rival 意为“对手；竞争者”，我记得的是赛事记录里测量过的那一位，1965 年打完了，至今仍被说成球场里最安静的一位。
rival 为抽象总称，母亲 1967 年说，对手是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的对手。
